subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline controls be added as shared MessagePresentation typed actions with an authenticated chat.callback RPC, and should any WebChat capability/config key be introduced despite retired WebChat config?
rationale: The first implementation defines a public Gateway/UI interaction contract, callback security semantics, and possibly a new config surface; automation should not choose those product and security boundaries unilaterally.

options.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
options.body: Use shared typed presentation actions, add a scoped authenticated chat.callback RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and make an explicit yes/no decision on WebChat capability config.

options.title: Protocol first, UI second
options.body: Approve the schema/RPC/auth contract as a first layer and leave Control UI rendering/click state for a follow-up issue or PR.

options.title: Defer interactive WebChat
options.body: Keep WebChat text-only for now and route broader reactions, feedback, and approval-card UX through a later WebUI interaction direction.

recommendation.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
recommendation.body: Use shared typed presentation actions, add a scoped authenticated chat.callback RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and make an explicit yes/no decision on WebChat capability config.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across WebChat config retirement, Gateway chat/protocol surfaces, docs, and UI routing decisions.
